name: The Herald Reel
tagline: A poster-wall movie-catalog for the worst Dota ever played — browse Herald disasters like Netflix tiles, zero text walls, zero AI smell.
concept: One persistent public "gallery" message per channel that the bot edits in place forever (UPDATE_MESSAGE type 7). The gallery is media-first: every page of the browser is a MediaGallery of bot-composited PNG "match posters" (Pillow composites of 5v5 hero portraits + scoreline + a networth sparkline burned into the image), with a thin Section list underneath whose accessory Buttons open matches. Drilling into a match swaps the same message to a "Poster" view: a big composited scoreboard image, two Section+Thumbnail standout-player cards with item app-emojis inline, and a matplotlib gold-lead chart with tower-death markers. Personal drilldowns (player cards, hero picker) are ephemeral so the channel never gains a second bot message. Everything is framed as a video-store catalog ("This week's reel", "Staff picks", lens = sort), never as an assistant. All hero/item iconography is application emojis (one-time 335-emoji seed) plus CDN hero portraits baked into composites; charts are dark-theme matplotlib PNGs attached via attachment:// in MediaGalleries.
message_layouts:
ASSET PIPELINE (prerequisite): (a) one-time seeding script uploads 127 hero icons (32x32, padded to 128x128) + ~208 item icons (88x64 padded square) as application emojis, slugs `h_<name>` / `i_<name>`, mapping stored in Postgres; (b) poster compositor (Pillow): 640x360 PNG per match — top row 5 radiant hero crops (heroes/crops/{name}.png 400x250 scaled), bottom row 5 dire crops, center strip "46:56 · 118 kills" text + winner banner + a 600x60 gold-lead sparkline; posters cached on disk keyed by match_id; (c) chart renderer (matplotlib Agg, facecolor #1e1f22, radiant gold #C8A951 fill above zero, dire red #C23C2A below, vertical tick markers for towerDeaths, x-axis minutes).

interaction_flow:
ENTRY: user @mentions the bot ("@Herald show me the reel") or any message in the bot's channel matching a trigger; bot posts ONE public Gallery Wall message and stores message_id → view-state in Postgres. All subsequent navigation edits that message; the channel never accumulates bot spam (hard requirement).

NAV RULES (strict): (1) Public message = edit-in-place ONLY, via interaction response type 6 DEFERRED_UPDATE_MESSAGE followed by PATCH /webhooks/{app_id}/{token}/messages/@original with multipart files — deferral is mandatory because poster/chart rendering can exceed 3s on cache miss (cache hit path may respond type 7 directly). On every PATCH, the `attachments` array lists exactly the files for the new view (omitted old attachments are dropped automatically — this is the mechanism for swapping posters between pages). (2) Personal drilldowns (player card, hero picker, "all builds") = ephemeral CHANNEL_MESSAGE_WITH_SOURCE flags 64|32768; ephemeral views page within themselves via type 7. (3) Anyone in the channel may click anything — state is per-message, not per-user; last click wins (fine for a small server, and it makes the widget feel like a shared jukebox).

FLOWS:
- Gallery ▸ lens select → same wall re-sorted, page reset to 1, 4 new posters attached. "By day — calendar" swaps to Calendar layout; "Hero hunt…" sends the ephemeral picker instead of editing.
- Gallery ▸ filter select (multi, max 3) → toggles filter chips, wall re-renders; "Clear all" resets. Active filters echoed in the header line ("showing Bloodiest · Thursday · 45+ min").
- Gallery ▸ ◀/▶ → page through 4-poster pages (12 pages at default lens; buttons disabled at bounds).
- Gallery ▸ Open (Section accessory) or 🎲 Surprise me → Match Poster view (random respects active filters).
- Calendar ▸ Browse Thursday → Gallery wall with Day:Thursday filter applied.
- Poster ▸ player select → ephemeral Player Card; ◀/▶ inside it cycles the ten players (edits ephemeral); the public Poster stays put underneath.
- Poster ▸ 📈 More graphs → Graphs view (edit); ◀ Back to match → Poster; ◀◀ Back to reel → Gallery wall restored to prior lens/filter/page (state row remembers it).
- Poster ▸ 🎲 Another one → new random Poster directly (browse-by-shuffle loop, the killer casual path).
- Hero picker ▸ pick → ephemeral confirms; public gallery re-renders hero-filtered via REST edit (bot has the message_id; no interaction token needed for the public message).
- 🔄 refresh → re-runs the current query (new matches ingested since last render).
- Staleness guard: if a click arrives for a match pruned from the DB, respond type 7 with the wall + a header line "That one aged out of the week — here's the current reel."

RENDER/CACHE: posters and charts are pure functions of match_id (+ view params) → PNG files cached on the Fly volume; first render of a page is ~1–2s for 4 cached posters, worst case ~6s cold (hence defer). Weekly prune deletes cached PNGs with their matches.
component_budget: Gallery Wall 27/40 (4 attachments), Calendar 33/40 (7 attachments), Match Poster 19/40 (2 attachments), Graphs 6/40 (4 attachments), Player Card ephemeral 11/40 (1 attachment), Hero Picker ephemeral 8/40 (1 attachment). Text budgets all ≤ ~1200 of 4000 chars (largest: Poster view incl. 10 select-option labels). Selects: lens 9 options, filter 16, player-inspect 10, hero-picker 25 — all ≤25. custom_ids ≤ ~40 chars. App emojis needed ≈ 335 of 2000 cap.
risks: 1) Render latency: every nav click on a cold page needs 4 composited PNGs — mandatory deferral + disk cache + pre-warming the first 3 pages of each lens at ingest time; if Fly's shared CPU makes matplotlib slow, pre-render all charts at ingest (2000 matches × ~4 charts is heavy — mitigate by only pre-rendering top-200 per lens). 2) PATCH attachment bookkeeping is fiddly (attachments array must exactly match the new view or files leak/vanish) — needs a single render→payload builder, never hand-rolled per view. 3) MediaGallery grid layout (2x2 vs strip) is client-decided by item count/aspect; posters must look right at both 4-up and 1-up — test on mobile early. 4) Shared state means two users clicking simultaneously race on one message; acceptable for a small server but 'last click wins' should be documented, and DEFERRED_UPDATE renders must re-read state at PATCH time. 5) One-time 335-emoji seed has undocumented rate limits — serial, 429-aware, budget hours worst case. 6) Ephemeral hero-pick editing the public message uses the bot-token REST edit, not the interaction token — requires MANAGE of its own message only (fine) but is a second code path to test. 7) The 46-min composite poster text baked into PNGs is unlocalizable/unscreen-readable — mirror key facts in Section TextDisplays (already done) and set MediaGallery alt descriptions.

name: The Herald Ledger
tagline: A card catalog for the worst games ever played — pick a shelf, open a drawer, pull a match.
concept: Group-by-first stat explorer disguised as a cozy library widget. One persistent public message per invocation ("the Ledger") that edits itself in place through four altitudes: SHELVES (pick a group-by dimension) → DRAWER (aggregate table + distribution chart for that dimension's buckets) → STACK (paged match list inside one bucket) → CARD (single match with networth chart, emoji rosters) → optional PLAYER REPORT CARD. Every view is a Container with matplotlib PNG attachments in MediaGalleries and app-emoji hero/item icons in TextDisplays. Zero AI framing: no prompts, no 'ask me anything', no personality — just tables, charts, selects and buttons, like a server stats widget. All navigation state is encoded in custom_id (stateless bot; e.g. `L|stack|dur=40p|s=kills|p=2`, well under 100 chars), so restarts cost nothing and anyone in the channel can drive anyone's Ledger (last click wins — it's a shared widget). Pull-only: the Ledger appears only when summoned; every interaction is UPDATE_MESSAGE (type 7) or deferred type 6 + PATCH, never a new channel post, except the explicit "Keep this one" pin button.
message_layouts:
ALL messages: flags 32768, single top-level Container. Charts are matplotlib PNGs sent as attachments and referenced via attachment:// in MediaGallery. Hero/item icons are application emojis `<:h_axe:ID>` / `<:i_blink:ID>` (seeded once from Steam CDN, ~335 emojis, 2000 cap). custom_id grammar: `L|<view>|<params>` — e.g. `L|shelf`, `L|drawer|hero|sort=played|hp=2`, `L|stack|dur=40p|s=kills|p=1`, `L|card|8888295980|from=dur40p.kills.1`, `L|player|8888295980|slot=7`, `L|rand`, `L|chaos`, `L|pin|8888295980`, `L|help`.

(5) Back-issue depth is limited by the DB's ~1-week retention — either persist weekly board snapshots (top-15 rows + pre-rendered charts) at week rollover, or the week select honestly offers only 1–2 issues. (6) Ephemeral chart responses require defer-then-PATCH-with-32768 (deferred type 5 only allows EPHEMERAL flag) — an implementation gotcha called out in the spec; getting it wrong 400s. (7) Pin-to-Fridge dedupe needs a tiny pins table keyed (week, match_id) or a message-scan — trivial but easy to forget.

- M0 "Browse Matches" → L0 (new ephemeral). M0 "Surprise Me" → L2 random match (new ephemeral, filters=defaults).

- L2 "Players" → L3a, "Networth" → L3b (defer+PATCH), "Items" → L3c, "◀ Results" → L1 at the SAME page (page is in custom_id), "Another random" → new random L2, "Filters" → L0, "OpenDota ↗" = link button, no interaction.
- L3a/b/c nav rows cross-link all three deep views + back to L2 + Home, so users hop Players↔Networth↔Items without climbing.

STATE: 100% encoded in custom_ids (filters, sort, page, match id, sub-view). No server-side session store; bot restarts and 15-min token expiry are non-issues because every click is a fresh interaction carrying full state. Ten users = ten ephemeral messages = zero contention. Ephemeral messages Discord garbage-collects on client restart — acceptable; user just clicks Browse again.

(2) Modal-submit → UPDATE_MESSAGE is inconsistently supported across client paths; spec mandates the always-valid defer(6)+PATCH @original route instead — do not ship the type-7 path without testing. (3) Editing an ephemeral interaction message with NEW attachments requires the multipart PATCH-@original route (discord.py: `InteractionResponse.defer()` then `interaction.edit_original_response(attachments=[File(...)])`); plain `edit_message(attachments=...)` on type 7 has historically been flaky with V2 flags in discord.py — pin discord.py ≥ 2.6 (first version with LayoutView/Container V2 support) and verify in the test server. name: The Match Board (Command Deck)
tagline: One pinned message that IS the entire UI — stacked selects, in-place edits, zero spam, zero AI smell.
concept: A single pinned Components-V2 message per channel ("the Board") that behaves like a channel-native dashboard widget. It has exactly three modes — BROWSE (filterable/groupable match list), GROUPED (aggregate rows), and DETAIL (one match with scoreboard + matplotlib chart) — and every interaction responds with UPDATE_MESSAGE (type 7) so the Board morphs in place and never posts a new message. State is shared (last click wins, like a jukebox in the corner of the bar), stored server-side in Postgres keyed by (channel_id, message_id); custom_ids are static verbs, never carry state except row-target ids. The nightly ingest silently edits the header counts and resets filters to defaults at 6 AM. Charts are matplotlib PNGs swapped via multipart PATCH on the interaction webhook (omitting old attachments drops them automatically). Hero/item icons render inline as application emojis with deliberately short names (<:h_pa:...>, <:i_bfury:...>) to survive the 4,000-char component-text ceiling. No slash commands, no AI copy, no "ask me anything" — it reads like a stats kiosk someone bolted into the channel.

ALL layouts are one message, flags 32768, everything inside a single Container (type 17). Emoji names are illustrative; real ids are 19-digit snowflakes. App-emoji names MUST be short slugs (h_pa, h_wk, i_bfury, i_mkb) — this is load-bearing for the char budget.

interaction_flow:
CREATION: Jenkins mentions the bot with "menu"/"board" → bot posts the Board (BROWSE, defaults: show=bloodiest, no filters, flat, page 1) and pins it (needs Manage Messages; if pin fails, log and continue — the Board still works unpinned). One Board per channel; a second request re-renders/reuses the stored (channel_id, message_id). If the message was deleted, recreate. Pull-only constraint holds: creation is mention-triggered; nightly refresh only EDITS (edits never ping).

EVERY component interaction → response type 7 UPDATE_MESSAGE (the Board edits itself). Exceptions: chart changes and any render that might exceed 3s → type 6 DEFERRED_UPDATE_MESSAGE then multipart PATCH /webhooks/{app_id}/{token}/messages/@original with payload_json + files[0]; "Someone else…" → type 9 MODAL; modal miss → type 4 + EPHEMERAL(64) + IS_COMPONENTS_V2(32768).

TRANSITIONS:
- board:show / board:day / board:len / board:hero (non-'other') → update state, reset page to 1, re-render current mode (BROWSE or GROUPED). Selecting a hero from GROUPED also flips to BROWSE.
- board:group → value none → BROWSE; hero/day/length → GROUPED page 1.
- board:page:prev|next → same mode, page ±1 (clamped; edge buttons disabled).
- board:view:{match_id} → DETAIL (chart=lead default). Deferred (type 6) because it attaches a PNG.
- board:drill:hero:{id} | drill:day:{date} | drill:len:{bucket} → set that filter, group=flat → BROWSE page 1.
- board:adj:prev|next (in DETAIL) → DETAIL of neighbor in the frozen filtered+sorted id list captured when entering DETAIL (stored in state so pagination is stable while browsing).
- board:random → DETAIL of a uniform-random match matching current filters (works from all three modes). If filters match 0 matches, BROWSE renders the empty state: sections replaced by one TextDisplay "Nothing matches — loosen a filter or hit ♻ Reset" (component count drops, still valid).
- board:back → BROWSE at the page containing the match just viewed.
- board:chart → deferred re-render of DETAIL with new PNG; only new file listed in attachments so the old chart is dropped.
- board:reset → defaults, BROWSE page 1.
- MODAL_SUBMIT board:hero:text → fuzzy hit: type 7 → BROWSE with hero set (UPDATE_MESSAGE is valid for modals launched from a component interaction); miss: ephemeral notice, Board untouched.

STATE & CONCURRENCY: one row in Postgres: board_state(channel_id PK, message_id, mode, show, day, len_flags[], hero_id, group_by, page, detail_match_id, detail_nav_ids[], chart_kind, updated_at). Interactions read-modify-write with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; renders are pure functions of state so a lost race just means the later click's render wins (self-healing). Shared state is a feature for this server size — the footer says so in plain words.

NIGHTLY (6 AM, after ingest/prune): recompute the week window and top-23 hero options, reset state to defaults, edit the Board in place. No send, no ping.

NEVER: no new channel messages, no threads, no followups except the single ephemeral hero-miss notice.
component_budget: BROWSE: 37/40 (1 container + 1 header + 3 separators + 5 select rows @2 = 10 + 5 match sections @3 = 15 + nav row 1+5 buttons = 6 + 1 footer). GROUPED: identical skeleton, 37/40. DETAIL: 15/40 (container, 3 TextDisplays, separator, MediaGallery, footnote, chart select row 2, nav row 1+5). Text budget: BROWSE ~2,300/4,000; DETAIL ~2,950/4,000 — the binding constraint is emoji markdown (~28 chars each × ~70 in DETAIL), hence mandatory short app-emoji slugs (h_pa, i_bfury) and a 3,600-char render-time guard that truncates the footnote first, then drops backpack/neutral items (already excluded), then falls back to hero names without item emojis.
risks: (1) Shared state: two users clicking within the same second race on UPDATE_MESSAGE — last write wins and renders are pure functions of DB state, so worst case is one user's view flickering to the other's filters; acceptable for a small server but must be stated in the footer or it feels haunted. (2) 4,000-char ceiling in DETAIL is real (~2,950 estimated with 70 emojis); if Discord counts select option labels/descriptions toward the total (undocumented), BROWSE's 25-option hero select adds ~1,200 chars and could breach — verify empirically in the spike and be ready to trim hero-option descriptions. (3) App-emoji seeding (~127 heroes + ~90 items actually referenced) is a one-time serial 429-aware job; emoji names in messages must exactly match uploaded names, so the slug map must live in the DB. (4) type-7 responses with new attachments require the deferred(6)+multipart PATCH path — discord.py's InteractionResponse.edit_message with files needs verification on the installed version; fall back to raw webhook PATCH. (5) Pinning needs Manage Messages; degrade gracefully. (6) V2 flag is one-way — never try to convert the Board back to a classic message; recreate instead. (7) 'Top 23 heroes' select recomputed nightly means option values change under a stale client; handle unknown select values by ignoring + re-rendering. (8) UPDATE_MESSAGE from MODAL_SUBMIT is only valid when the modal came from a component interaction — true here, but if it 400s in practice, respond type 6 then PATCH @original.

name: THE HERALD MACHINE
tagline: A slot machine for terrible Dota. Pull the lever, get a disaster, keep the good ones.
concept: One persistent public message per session that behaves like an arcade cabinet. The default action is a giant PULL THE LEVER button that edits the message through a two-frame "reel spin" animation into a match card: a punchy 3-line hook built from real stats, a networth-swing chart PNG, and a deterministic template "verdict" with a fire rating. A themed-pull select ("Feed me a feeder", "The throw", "Troll build roulette") is the menu board for people with a craving. Re-roll is always one click. Drill-in (full scoreboard → per-player shopping-log card) and a filterable Browse mode exist for the 10% who want control, but the machine is optimized for the person who doesn't know what they want. Zero AI framing anywhere: verdicts are rule-based templates, copy reads like a carnival cabinet, hero/item icons are app emojis. Everything edits in place — exactly one bot message exists until a user explicitly clicks 📌 Keep, which mints a compact permanent card (user-initiated, so the no-spam rule holds).

CUSTOM_ID SCHEME: `hm:<action>[:<arg>]`. Session state (mode, active match, filters, page, sort, theme) lives in Postgres keyed by the machine message_id. All app emojis pre-seeded (127 heroes + ~208 items ≈ 335 of 2000 cap); `<:pa:…>` below means the app emoji for that hero/item.
